newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PSE recovers from early losses to close up.
newsitem.headline: Czech PSE recovers from early losses to close up.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange, led by strong gains to several blue chip issues, recovered from early losses to close slightly higher on Friday.
SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- the market's three most-capitalised issues -- rose in late trading to reverse the early trend of the PX50 index, which closed 0.6 points higher at 557.4.
Engineering concern Skoda shares also rebounded, dropping 23 crowns at the daily price fixing and then rallying to close down three at 1,022.
Despite breaking its three-session declining streak, analysts said prices of many blue chips were reaching fairly valued levels, making the prospect of further strong market gains dim at best.
"Right now we're seeing very little foreign participation, people are becoming more realistic again because the blue chips are pretty fairly valued," said Jan Sykora of Wood and Company.
Overall, 183 issues closed higher, while 149 lost ground and 94 held steady. Total volume was 835,072 shares on turnover of 571.3 million crowns.
"On the P/E level, the market may look cheaper than Poland or Hungary, but on earnings growth it does not look quite as attractive."
Broader issues PVT and Ceske Radiokomunikace led net decliners at the fixing, losing 191 and 188 crowns respectively.
Dealers added that the country's macro-economic performance, which has sagged in recent months has also helped turn investor attentions elsewhere in the region.
